metadata-description: A practical starting point for public agencies, civil-society organizations, and NGOs exploring Ethereum as open public infrastructure.
hero-description: Explore whether an open, shared public layer can give people and institutions more independence, verifiability, and control than a single operator can.
intro: Public agencies, multilateral organizations, civil-society groups, and NGOs can use Ethereum to explore durable infrastructure for coordination, records, payments, and credentials.
mission-description: The question is not whether to put a service onchain. Start with the public problem, the people affected, and the degree of independence, verifiability, and control it needs.
infrastructure-card-description: Identity, records, payments, data exchange, and long-lived civic systems.
civil-society-card-description: Public goods, transparent funding, humanitarian work, connectivity, and local coordination.
policy-card-description: Sovereignty, inclusion, privacy, accountability, vendor dependence, and exit paths.
evidence-card-description: Primary-source case studies and research to assess in context.
standard-description: Technology does not make a service legitimate by itself. Public-interest deployment should protect privacy, accessibility, agency, and recourse; be understandable enough to govern; and remain usable if an integrator, provider, or funder changes course.
